visual_brief.subject: A production MCP gateway separating multiple tenants while controlling agent-to-tool traffic
verified_context: Red Hat made its MCP gateway generally available in Connectivity Link 1.5 with dedicated and shared isolation patterns.
The gateway supports protocol negotiation between stateless and earlier stateful MCP transports while federating tools, prompts, and selected resources.
Structured audit logs, Prometheus metrics, and an external NeMo Guardrails integration provide separate observability and content-policy controls.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: A shared gateway can centralize policy while preserving separate traffic paths and operational boundaries for multiple agent-tool tenants.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: A monumental layered gatehouse with several sealed chambers and one controlled terracotta passage branching into isolated corridors.

candidate_notes.A: Constitution-compliant. The frontal gatehouse and three chambers communicate separation, but the retained objects in each chamber compete with the traffic-path metaphor.
candidate_notes.B: Selected. A single controlled path branches over four physically separated wells, preserving the gateway threshold and tenant isolation at thumbnail and cover crops.
candidate_notes.C: Constitution-compliant. The circular compound expresses isolation, but human figures and landscape detail reduce the clarity of the gateway path at small size.

crop_review.article_desktop: The central gate and all four isolated wells remain visible in the wide crop.
crop_review.article_mobile: A centered narrow cover crop keeps the primary gate, intersection, and two deep separated wells.
crop_review.thumbnail: The terracotta path and dark isolated wells remain distinct at 320px wide.

golden_reference_comparison: The selected image matches the production archive's warm field, architectural mass, sparse terracotta emphasis, physical depth, and strong central silhouette while using a story-specific gateway composition.
